messages:
Maria G.: Heads-up — on the fp8 activation canary I started seeing subtle correctness drift in chat-model sims. Perplexity went 3.2 -> 3.9 after the rollout, and a few production-like traces show token-sampling instability.
Jonathan H.: I repro'd locally. nvprof / tracer shows we pick the fp8_matmul kernel after calibration, but wall-time is worse for seq_len > 1024. Numbers below from perf run (batch=1, seq=1536):
```
fp16 path:  tokens/s = 210
fp8 path:   tokens/s = 150  (kernel chosen: matmul_fp8_v2)
matmul_fp8_v2 time = 6.7 ms  vs 4.2 ms (fp16)
```
This didn't used to be slower.
Alex K.: Small repro attached — the real problem looks like a scale mismatch in the activation->KV write path. When we quantize activation for matmul we use per-tensor calibration, but the KV cache writer expects the "matrix scale" from per-channel calibration. The result: cached keys have a different implicit scale and get treated as stale, causing extra conversions. Snippet from my debug log: 
```
[debug] kv_cache: write scale=0.00321
[debug] matmul: act_scale=0.00273
[warn] kv_cache: scale mismatch, invalidating entry
```
That invalidation shows up as a lot more memory churn and recompute.
Kevin S.: Reproduced on a 4090 with our nightly. Also saw an assert in mixed_matmul.cc when BF16 fallback gets chosen: 
```
Assertion `A.shape[1] == B.shape[0]' failed in mixed_matmul.cc:line 412
```
looks like an ordering/transpose bug when we apply channel-wise scales during pack.
perf-bot: build 2345 succeeded :white_check_mark:
ci-bot: bisect started between commits 6b2f1a3 -> 8c4d9f0; testing range (automated)

Maria G.: Hypothesis: calibration mode mismatch + packing transpose bug. When we changed default calibration to per-channel for weights but left activations per-tensor, the runtime kernel selector didn't propagate the effective scale metadata to the KV writer. On top of that, the matmul kernel has a special-case transpose path for FP8->BF16 that assumes packed layout; if scales are applied in the wrong loop order it can index incorrectly.
Jonathan H.: Quick profiling shows extra memcpy and quant/dequant ops in the fp8 path:
```
profile summary (fp8): memcpy 38ms, quantize 12ms, matmul 6.7ms, dequant 10ms
profile summary (fp16): memcpy 20ms, matmul 4.2ms
```
So overhead is not pure matmul kernel time — conversion+cache invalidation dominates for long sequences.
Alex K.: Minimal repro script (python) attached. Config that triggers it: 
```
model_config:
  quantization:
    activations: fp8
    weights: int8
    activation_calibration: per_tensor   # causes mismatch with weights per_channel
    weight_calibration: per_channel
```
Workaround: set activation_calibration: per_channel and restart canary -> tokens/s returns to expected range.
Kevin S.: But if we force per_channel for activations we see higher memory and slightly worse quality on a few evals. Need a proper fix.
Maria G.: Action items: 
- revert canary flag `fp8-activation-rollout` (owner: @Kevin S.)
- add metadata propagation for effective_scale on request path so KV writer sees the exact quant params (owner: @Jonathan H.)
- fix transpose/pack ordering in mixed_matmul to guard against inconsistent scale application (owner: @Alex K.)
- add unit/regression test that runs seq_len 1536 on fp8 path (owner: @Maria G.)

Jonathan H.: I'll open a PR for the metadata propagation and a small perf test. Bisect pointed to commit 8c4d9f0 (quantization: switch default calibration to per-channel) as the first bad revision.
Alex K.: I'll add an assert to detect scale mismatch earlier and a fallback that avoids invalidating the whole KV cache (cheap fix: quantize-on-write with saved scale tag).

Maria G.: For visibility, creating issue: https://redwood.internal/infra/issue/INF-4712 and adding eng-runtime + eng-ml. Reverting canary now. :thumbsup:
Kevin S.: Revert flag pushed to canary cluster. Rolling back in 5m. I'll follow up with perf runs after revert and post numbers.

Maria G.: Thanks team — after revert we should triage the PRs and get a non-breaking fix before re-enabling fp8 activation by default. Keep notes in INF-4712 and drop important logs in the issue thread.
